# What `jq -cS` renders each adversarial scalar as, and what this crate must
# render it as to keep `remote_hash` stable.
#
# GENERATED by running the pinned jq — never asserted from memory. The widely
# cited `1.0` -> `1` canonicalisation is jq 1.6 behaviour; 1.7 preserves the
# literal of a number it does not operate on, which is why this file records
# the version it was taken against.
#
# jq version: jq-1.7.1
# generator:  printf '{"fields":{"description":<literal>}}' | jq -cS '.fields.description'
#
# The bash oracle runs on whatever jq the USER has, so a divergence here is a
# divergence against one pinned version, not against every one.
#
# Columns: literal <TAB> jq <TAB> verdict <TAB> note
# verdict `match` means this crate must produce the jq column byte for byte;
# `divergence` means it must not, and the note says why that is accepted.

1	1	match	a plain integer
0	0	match	zero
-0	-0	match	negative zero
9007199254740993	9007199254740993	match	beyond f64's exact integer range
100000000000000000000	100000000000000000000	match	beyond i64 and u64
1.0	1.0	match	a whole-valued float
1.500	1.500	match	trailing zeros a re-render would drop
0.1	0.1	match	not exactly representable in binary
3.141592653589793238462643383279	3.141592653589793238462643383279	match	more digits than f64 holds
1e999	1E+999	divergence	an exponent beyond f64's range
1e2	1E+2	divergence	exponent notation
1e-5	0.00001	divergence	a small negative exponent
"plain"	"plain"	match	a plain string
""	""	match	the empty string
"tab\there"	"tab\there"	match	a short-escape control
"nul\u0000here"	"nul\u0000here"	match	U+0000
"unit\u001fhere"	"unit\u001fhere"	match	U+001F
"del\u007fhere"	"del\u007fhere"	divergence	U+007F
"emoji \ud83d\ude00"	"emoji 😀"	match	a non-BMP character as a surrogate pair
"slash a\/b"	"slash a/b"	match	an escaped forward slash
null	null	match	null
true	true	match	true
[1.500,2]	[1.500,2]	match	a number inside an array
{"b":1.500,"a":2}	{"a":2,"b":1.500}	match	a number inside an object, keys unsorted
